title: Investigate why async Processing on SIT/UAT feels far slower than expected without colliding with Claude's W5-12 implementation lane
lane: Copilot - deploy / runtime / queue / environment investigation
objective: Find where the slowdown actually happens in the live async Processing path: queue pickup, retry behavior, OCR runtime, extraction runtime, Stage C cascade runtime, or environment drift between SIT and UAT. Return hard evidence and a narrow fix recommendation, while leaving Claude's W5-12 product implementation lane untouched.
why_this_is_copilot_lane: The latest proof artifact shows the task stayed pending with stage=null before OCR/extract began, which points first to worker pickup / queue / retry / runtime environment, not to a pure frontend issue.
Comparing SIT and UAT runtime behavior, worker health, queue latency, and deployed env/config drift is deploy/runtime work.
Claude is already assigned to W5-12 product implementation and should not be pulled off into infra/runtime diagnosis unless Copilot proves the issue is actually app-code logic.
known_evidence: In test-results/w5-copilot-batch-deploy-sit-proof-03/.../summary.json, POST /api/v1/tasks/process-document returned a task id, but repeated GET /api/v1/tasks/{id} stayed status=pending, stage=null, result=null for multiple polls.
In the same artifact, the document list still showed status=uploaded during those polls, which suggests the worker had not yet started or had not persisted processing state.
The current async path is Celery-based: /api/v1/tasks/process-document -> process_document.delay() -> worker task -> run_pipeline().

The current pipeline is heavier than older direct runs because it can execute OCR -> extraction -> Stage C cascade -> reconciliation -> journal mapping, and Stage C can call multiple models sequentially.
what_to_do: 1. Reproduce the slowdown on SIT and, if available, UAT using the real async Processing path rather than only the synchronous /process path.

2. Capture exact timestamps for: request accepted, task enqueued, task first visible as started/progress, OCR start/end, extraction start/end, Stage C start/end, mapping start/end, document status persisted to processing/review_scan/failed.
3. Inspect Celery worker health, queue backlog, retry activity, and result-backend behavior for the processing task IDs involved.

4. Compare SIT vs UAT runtime configuration that materially affects latency: worker concurrency, result backend, Redis health, object-storage download latency, OCR engine availability, and the actual effective env values used by the live containers.
5. Determine whether the main problem is before pipeline start (queue/worker), during OCR, during extraction, during Stage C cascade, or during persistence.
6. Return the smallest credible fix path: runtime-only fix for Copilot, or app-code fix to hand back to Claude/Codex if and only if the evidence points there.

allowed_scope: Openclaw workflow runs and deploy/runtime investigation
Minimal diagnostic scripts or logs collection
forbidden_scope: Do not implement W5-12 line-item storage, review UI, or export-realdata product changes
Do not refactor src/frontend/main-ux-ui.html or src/frontend/index.html for W5-12
Do not modify application behavior in ways that would overlap with Claude's line-item/export lane unless the evidence proves a tiny runtime-safe fix is the real cause and you clearly isolate it
Do not claim W5-12 is fixed or in scope for this investigation

questions_to_answer: Is the major delay happening before the worker picks up the task, or after the pipeline begins?
If before pickup, what exactly is the blocker: worker offline, low concurrency, queue backlog, retries, Redis/result-backend lag, or storage-download failure causing delayed retries?
If after pickup, which stage dominates wall-clock time: OCR, extraction, Stage C cascade, or mapping?
Is UAT actually faster than SIT on the same kind of document, and if so, what runtime difference explains it?
Is there a regression window in git history or deployed config that explains why users remember it as under 1 minute?
acceptance_criteria: The report identifies the dominant slowdown stage with concrete evidence, not guesswork.
The report clearly separates queue/worker delay from OCR/LLM processing delay.
If UAT and SIT differ, the report states exactly what differs and why it matters.
If a fix is recommended, it is scoped to the responsible lane: Copilot for runtime/deploy fixes, Claude/Codex for app-code fixes.
The report explicitly states that W5-12 remains a separate product lane and was not modified by this task.

final_instruction_to_copilot: Investigate the live slowdown and return hard evidence. Do not drift into W5-12 implementation. Your job is to say where the time is really going and what lane should fix it next.
